main_text.p: am diligenter concinnare studuerunt: tamen chreiam & grammaticum sensum nos quidem, quantum dabit Deus, persequemur.

Videtur Propheta noster persuasum habuisse, futurum ut tota ciuitas uel terra dehiscente absorberetur: uel (ut olim accidit Pentapoli) igne & sulphure cœlitus depluente, incendio absumeretur: uel alia ratione deleta, fieret miserabile πολυ-ἀνθρώπων[?] incolarum. Fuit autem hæc persuasio minus digna tanto uiro, quem nō fugiebat, Deum in resipiscentes non ita, ut in eos qui sunt ἀμετανόητοι, animaduertere: sed poenas uel mitigare, uel etiam prorsus relaxare: ac piorum esse, gratulari aliis resipiscentiæ donum, & liberationem à malo.
main_text.head: THESIS DE SOLITARIA VITA.
main_text.p: Nequaquā eum ad modum dolori indulgendum nobis est, ut hominum contubernium & uestigia derelinquetes, nō tam quid ipsi agamus, quidue præstare debeamus, quàm quid aliis sit euenturū, μετεωριζόμενοι exspectemus.

page.notes: Greek words are uncertain at two points. "πολυ-ἀνθρώπων" (line 6) is a best reading and marked [?]. "ἀμετανόητοι" (line 9) is read from the context of "animaduertere" but the glyphs are small. Several long s are rendered as plain s. The printed hyphen in "legiti-" is kept because the word continues on the next page, where the catchword "mæ&c" indicates the next word begins. The printed "Nequaquā" and "dolori" join is as printed. The heading level 2 is chosen because it is a title above a passage.
